name: GitHub
summary: Creating a GitHub OAuth App (or GitHub App) is self-serve and takes minutes, with no review. The main decision is OAuth App vs GitHub App, and the main risk is that one OAuth App allows only one callback URL.

verdict.label: Easy
verdict.headline: Self-serve in about 10 minutes. No review unless you list on GitHub Marketplace.

approvalWait.appliesWhen: never for private use; Marketplace listing is a separate, optional review

agent: Pick OAuth App vs GitHub App based on whether you need fine-grained repo permissions
Prepare the form values: app name, homepage, callback URL, scopes
Run the authorization-code flow against your callback once you paste the client_id
human: Sign in to GitHub (and pass 2FA) to open Developer settings
Click 'Register application' and copy the client secret into your secret store
Approve the app for your organization if the org restricts third-party OAuth apps

steps.title: Choose OAuth App or GitHub App
steps.detail: OAuth Apps act as the user with broad scopes (repo, user). GitHub Apps have fine-grained permissions, short-lived tokens and per-repo installation. For an agent acting on a user's repos, a GitHub App is usually the better long-term choice; OAuth Apps are simpler to start with.

steps.title: Open Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New
steps.detail: Requires a signed-in GitHub account. For an org-owned app, use the organization's settings instead.

steps.title: Fill in the registration form
steps.detail: Application name, homepage URL, and one Authorization callback URL. A callback on a subdirectory of the registered URL is accepted; a different host is not.

evidence.note: Callback URL rules from 'Authorizing OAuth apps'

steps.title: Generate a client secret
steps.detail: Shown once. Store it in your secret manager, never in the repo.

steps.title: Test the authorization-code flow
steps.detail: Send a user to /login/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, scope and state, then exchange the code at /login/oauth/access_token. Ask for Accept: application/json, or the token comes back form-encoded.

evidence.note: GitHub's 2FA mandate; not specific to OAuth apps

requirements.note: OAuth Apps allow exactly one callback URL. Use separate apps for dev, staging and prod.
Orgs with OAuth app access restrictions must approve your app before it can see org resources.
Only needed to sell or list publicly on GitHub Marketplace.

scopes.name: repo
scopes.purpose: Full read/write to private repos. Very broad; consider a GitHub App instead

endpoints.refreshTokens: OAuth Apps: no (tokens don't expire). GitHub Apps: yes, opt-in
endpoints.tokenLifetime: OAuth App: until revoked · GitHub App: 8h

blockers.symptom: 'The redirect_uri is not associated with this application'
blockers.cause: Host or port differs from the single registered callback.
blockers.fix: Register a separate OAuth App per environment, or use a GitHub App, which allows up to 10 callback URLs.

blockers.symptom: User authorized, but the API returns 404 on org repos
blockers.cause: The org has OAuth app access restrictions.
blockers.fix: An org owner approves the app under Org settings → Third-party access.

gotchas.title: Fake client_ids aren't rejected before login
gotchas.detail: GitHub redirects to /login before it validates client_id, so you can't confirm an app exists without a signed-in browser.

gotchas.title: OAuth App tokens never expire
gotchas.detail: Great for agents, but a leaked token is valid until revoked. Store it encrypted and support revocation.

uncertainties: Marketplace review duration isn't published; reports range from days to weeks.
